LLM Voice
body_text: LLM Voice Refactoring Agile Architecture About Thoughtworks Topics Architecture Refactoring Agile Delivery Microservices Data Testing DSL about me About Books FAQ content Videos Content Index Fragments Board Games Photography Thoughtworks Home Insights Careers Radar Engineering follow RSS Mastodon LinkedIn Bluesky X BGG LLM Voice 29 October 2026 Martin Fowler Sometimes when I read a post, I get the growing feeling that I'm reading the output of an LLM. I can't necessarily define why, although there are the common tells (it's not the em-dashes, it's the load-bearing tapestries). As I do this my desire to read on atrophies, sometimes to the point of revulsion There are tools out there that claim to be able to tell the difference between LLM-written prose and the old-fashioned biological product. I'm wary of them, partly due skeptism about their accuracy, but also because it rather misses the point. The reaction to LLM-Voice is a human one, that sense that we are in an uncanny valley of prose. By the time I'd reach for a tool to tell me what I'm reading, it's already too late, even if it confidently tells me there's no LLM present. I'm also suspicious of my own ability to accurately recognize LLM voice. Language changes over time, so a common sign of age is complaining about the language of the youngs. I'm inclined to bristle at prose that talks about âadopting a new sales motion ,â or âa sharp round-up of newsâ. But I've heard these constructs coming out of human mouths, so that's more a generational difference rather than between carbon and silicon. (And as a transplanted Brit, don't get me started on Americanisms, I'm sure I'll get used to them momentarily.) Right now I urge authors to be extra-wary of LLM-Voice. In particular I strongly recommend that authors should not fall into the trap of getting the LLM to write a draft. Even if it's edited by a human, it's very hard to expel the LLM-Voice - thus causing the uncanny valley reaction. 1 Even accepting suggestions of rephrasing is dangerous. I have heard of people using LLMs to develop outline and structure, that may be ok, but only as far as an outline. 2 Authors should fill the prose themselves. 1: Very hard, but not impossible. I've come across one case where I do know the first draft was entirely done by LLM, but I detected no LLM Voice when I read the final piece. It did, however, need a professional editor at a major periodical publication to clean it up. 2: My policy on this site, is that anyone who uses AI to help them write should declare how they used it, usually in the acknowledgments. This is partly for transparency, and partly so that readers can learn useful ways to use AI. In my own case, I don't use AI for generating prose, nor for help in structure. The only way I use it for writing is as a search tool (but I verify any information by going to the source). Say Your Writing is even more important in the age of LLMs. I habitually speak the words in my head and then write them down (and then edit what I've just written). This advice is particularly important to anyone who has any desire to communicate regularly with writing. Like many things, learning to be a good writer relies on lots of practice. It's a skill worth the time to acquire, but surrendering to an LLM will undermine any progress. In time it may be that LLMs will be so good that we can't tell the difference. In many ways, that's more worrying. Like most writers, I find writing an almost-essential tool for thinking. Often it's only by writing something down, that I can really get my thoughts on a topic into coherence. I've often started an essay knowing I don't really understand something, but the act of wrestling with the words forces me to overcome my confusions. As more people delegate writing to LLMs they will also delegate thinking and comprehension to LLMs. I don't want to do that, where's the fun of writing then? Although avoiding LLM-Voice is a general rule, it isn't an absolute one. An important example is that of Jim Highsmith (who contributes to this site). He finds working with an LLM is essential to his writing to overcome the bane of Parkinson's disease . I'll gladly deal with LLM-Voice in order to continue imbibing my old friend's wisdom. A more awkward case is that of translation. Many of my colleagues aren't comfortable in English, it is their second or fourth language. Some have found LLM translation an important part to their communication with those of us who know rather less Marathi. But I also would prefer rather a genuine human's clunky prose to the smooth but soulless LLM. There are situations where it would be reasonable for even a native Englishman to let LLMs write the prose. Such as if I'm writing a form letter to an official, or preparing a report I suspect no-one will ever read 3 . Maybe most documentation in the future will only be read by LLMs, and they won't have my uncanny valley worries. But if I want to communicate with humans, my humanity has to shine (or at least ooze) out of my prose. 3: Michael Nygard commented: âThere you really aren't trying to communicate thoughts from one person to other people. You're communicating with a process rather than a human. A human may open the envelope but that person is acting as a component in a cybernetic organism.â Notes 1: Very hard, but not impossible. I've come across one case where I do know the first draft was entirely done by LLM, but I detected no LLM Voice when I read the final piece. It did, however, need a professional editor at a major periodical publication to clean it up. 2: My policy on this site, is that anyone who uses AI to help them write should declare how they used it, usually in the acknowledgments. This is partly for transparency, and partly so that readers can learn useful ways to use AI. In my own case, I don't use AI for generating prose, nor for help in structure. The only way I use it for writing is as a search tool (but I verify any information by going to the source). 3: Michael Nygard commented: âThere you really aren't trying to communicate thoughts from one person to other people. You're communicating with a process rather than a human. A human may open the envelope but that person is acting as a component in a cybernetic organism.â Acknowledgements Alessio Ferri, Caer Sanders, Ian Cartwright, Jie Jessie Xia, Joshua Kerievsky, Michael Feathers, Michael Nygard, Scott Davies, and Wei Zhang commented on drafts of this post. I did not use AI or LLMs in any way while writing this post. Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) Built for Coders, Trusted by Defenders. Back to Blog Share this post Copy url to clipboard Copied Thinking Summary Mistral released Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), a 1-trillion-parameter multimodal model, now available with improved coding, cybersecurity, and reasoning efficiency. It leads open-weight benchmarks in coding and defensive security while offering three reasoning modes for cost-performance balance. Fully open-weight and European-trained, it empowers sovereign AI with customizable, self-hosted deployment options. We release the weights of Le Chonk, advancing the frontier of open models in agentic coding and cybersecurity. Earlier this month, we released Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), our flagship 1-trillion-parameter, natively multimodal model, in public preview. The response to the preview has exceeded our expectations, and we're grateful to our developer community, early-access customers, and partners for their support, collaboration, and feedback. Since then, we've put that feedback to work while continuing to scale reinforcement learning, driving massive improvements in coding and defensive cybersecurity . Gains continue to accelerate, with no signs of saturation. Today, we're releasing the weights of this improved Mistral Large 4. The new model also features substantial gains in reasoning efficiency that give developers greater performance while lowering inference costs. Mistral Large 4 ranks as the best open-weight model for coding and among the world's most capable open models overall. Trained from scratch on European infrastructure with clear lineage from inception to release, it gives organizations a trusted foundation for Sovereign AI Mistral is defining the sovereign AI category and leading the open frontier. We're committed to building the world's most capable models and releasing them openly, giving developers, enterprises, and institutions the power to own, customize, and control their AI. Built for the Builders. Mistral Large 4 entered public preview with strong results across leading coding benchmarks. Just three weeks of additional reinforcement learning have since propelled it to the forefront of open-weight coding, taking the lead on FrontierCode and Terminal-Bench while matching the best open-weight models on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index with substantially greater token efficiency. On Cognition's private FrontierCode 2.0 benchmark, which assesses end-to-end code quality and whether a repository maintainer would merge the agent's change, Mistral Large 4 leads with a score of 19.7%. Mistral Large 4 delivers frontier coding performance with significantly fewer tokens, making sophisticated coding agents more economical to run at scale. On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Mistral Large 4 scores 48%, effectively tied with the leading open-weight model, GLM-5.3, while using 47% fewer tokens per task on average. Built for the Defenders. Since its preview, we've been working with leading cybersecurity vendors to evaluate Mistral Large 4 in real-world environments to test Mistral Large 4’s strengths in vulnerability reproduction and patching. Mistral Large 4 scores 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, which measures a model’s ability to discover vulnerabilities in a codebase, reproduce and validate them, and patch them without breaking existing functionality. Crucially, Mistral Large 4 handles these legitimate defensive security tasks without unnecessary refusals. Our model’s built-in guardrails distinguishes between defensive and malicious, offensive cybersecurity tasks. It retains strong performance on Cyber benchmarks, while achieving an average refusal rate of 96.6% on malicious cyber requests, the highest we measure among open models. The model was able to match vulnerability detection recall rates against other frontier cyber models with a compelling cost curve. And, Mistral's support for model customization and data-sovereign deployment also lets us tailor it for our mission needs and client environments with strict data-residency requirements. We look forward to working with Mistral to strengthen critical infrastructure around the globe. Brad Medairy, President National Cyber at Booz Allen Hamilton Organizations that treat transparency and openness as strengths are positioned well as AI becomes central to security operations. Open-weight cybersecurity models extend that transparency to enterprises and governments that need to host and customize AI under their own control, and they allow researchers to study how these models behave, including where they could be misused. As adversaries increasingly use AI to accelerate their operations, we aim to work alongside model developers such as Mistral to help security teams build on that control, establishing a foundation for resilience by design rather than reactive threat management. Amy Chang, Head of Cisco's AI Threat Intelligence and Security Research When threats move at machine speed, human defense cannot keep pace. Worse, a defense you don’t control isn’t defense—it’s exposure. Security teams perform best when they take the steering wheel. Mistral's ML4 lets defenders audit the architecture, deploy on their own infrastructure, and keep full sovereignty. Resilience starts with autonomy, and open-weight models help give organizations the control to lead their own defense." Stephanie Cohen, Chief Strategy Officer at Cloudflare Powerful AI models alone won't tip the scales in cybersecurity. It takes deep security expertise, real-world threat intelligence, and rigorous testing. Our work with Mistral Large 4 tests how well frontier AI can reason through complex vulnerabilities, accelerate remediation, and ensure defenders move faster than adversaries. Dr. Bartley Richardson, Chief AI and Autonomous Systems Officer, CrowdStrike Elastic gives security teams the freedom to bring the AI they trust to the data they control, including Mistral’s open models, which are supported on Elastic Security today. We’ve already evaluated ML4 against real cybersecurity workloads, where models need to reason across complex data to help analysts make informed investigation and response decisions. This demonstrates the partnerships we are building to deliver powerful, open-weight models combined with the security context, transparency and control our customers demand. James Spiteri, Senior Director, Product Management, Elastic ENISA is experimenting with closed and open weight models in order to better understand their cyber capabilities. Open-weight models allow organisations to keep control of the technology their resilience depends on. ENISA access to and are testing Mistral Large 4 to identify security vulnerabilities, to audit code and analyse defensive logs. Laura Heuvinck, Head of Communications of ENISA We believe open-weight AI models have an important role to play in advancing cybersecurity by giving organizations greater flexibility, choice, and control. Innovations like Mistral Large 4 represent promising steps forward in AI's potential to transform cyber defense. We see continued AI innovation as an important opportunity to strengthen cybersecurity and help organizations navigate an evolving threat landscape. John Whittle, Chief Operating Officer at Fortinet Open models let security researchers and developers inspect, adapt and build on AI. Mistral is expanding what the ecosystem can build, and our collaboration on NVIDIA accelerated infrastructure helps developers put these models to work. Kari Briski, VP of Open Models and Software, NVIDIA As threats become ever faster, industrialized and now automated, defense must operate at a different scale. Volume, speed, trust: these are the three challenges facing cybersecurity in the age of AI. With Mistral AI, we are building European cyber AI, trained by our experts and operated under their control. By combining the power of AI, the expertise of our teams and our Cyber Threat Intelligence, we are accelerating our response so that we can protect more broadly, more quickly and with trusted European technology. Hugues Foulon, CEO of Orange Cyberdefense Rubrik supports Mistral and the push for ‘sovereign AI,’ to give European governments and regulated industries a credible option that does not route their data to other countries. Customers want model choices, including open-weight and private models, to support data residency, latency, cost and capability requirements. As part of our focus to deliver cyber resilience and speed recovery from both AI-powered attacks outside an organization and internal agents, we’ll continue rigorous cybersecurity testing with Mistral Large 4 and work closely together to serve evolving regional demands. Anneka Gupta, Chief Product Officer of Rubrik. As enterprises bring AI into production, they increasingly want models they can run on their own terms, with clear visibility into model behavior, data access, and agent permissions. Mistral Large 4 brings strong cybersecurity and technical reasoning to open weight AI, and many European enterprises are already embracing it as their sovereign model of choice. Zscaler Security for AI offerings, delivered on our sovereign Zero Trust Exchange in Europe, now integrate with Mistral, helping organizations continuously test their AI deployments, map what every model and agent can reach, and enforce policy inline. Together, we are empowering enterprises to adopt sovereign AI with the visibility, control, and data protection they need to innovate securely. Dhawal Sharma, EVP of AI and Data Security, Zscaler In the time since the preview, we carefully monitored cybersecurity-related use in our live traffic. Though we observed the model refusing to comply with black-box attacks against live targets, we see a potential for uplift to conduct real attacks. We are modifying our guardrails accordingly, and will continue updating them in the months to come. We are also providing enterprise design partners such as Orange Cyberdefense, with preview access to a specialized variant of Mistral Large 4 optimized for advanced cybersecurity workflows, including penetration testing, vulnerability assessment, and red-teaming. Access is subject to rigorous vetting and contractual safeguards, with testing restricted to owned or explicitly authorized systems in controlled environments. Meanwhile, customers are tailoring Mistral Large 4 with proprietary security data, policies, detection logic, and threat environments using Mistral Forge . For well-defined cybersecurity tasks, it can be further optimized into smaller, task-specific variants for greater accuracy, making security applications more effective. Learn more about sovereign AI for cybersecurity and how to work with us. Built for Work. Mistral Large 4 has continued improving on a range of broad enterprise-use metrics. For finance-related work , we improved the model’s ability to perform real-world workflows, especially ones involving the creation and editing of spreadsheets for finance and accounting use cases. This is reflected in our Finch scores climbing to 73.3%, second only to Kimi K3 for open models. Our RL pipeline enabled us to reach 84.5% on BrowseComp (starting from an SFT checkpoint that was achieving 75%). Whether deployed to internal members or external users, agents shouldn’t open you up to threats like system prompt exfiltration or malicious code injection. RL increased our gains on the B3 Agent Security Benchmark, with Mistral Large 4 resisting 97.1% of attacks vs 93.3% in Preview. This places it at the top of the OSS frontier, meaning anyone hosting the model can run a safe agent without additional tuning. For a public and citizen bank, technological sovereignty is not optional; it is a key prerequisite for maintaining our customers' trust. The introduction of this open model unlocks new opportunities and use cases. By partnering with Mistral AI, our ambition is to combine the best of human expertise and digital technology to deliver an enhanced experience of both customers and employees over the long term. Zakaria Moursli, Executive Vice President, Operational Performance, Payments and Digital Services, La Banque Postale See it in Action Cyber Vulnerability Triage : an agent reads incoming vulnerability reports, investigates the source code and product context, reproduces the flaws in an isolated sandbox, then writes and iterates on a patch until a canary exploit no longer works. Agentic webdev: with no human help, Mistral Large 4 builds Orbital Trace, a live 3D map of roughly 19,000 satellites and debris pieces orbiting Earth. It pulls real tracking data, writes the app, uses it in a browser to catch its own bugs and slowdowns, then fixes what an independent reviewer flags until all requirements pass. Quantum chemistry solver: Mistral Large 4 writes, from scratch, software that calculates where electrons sit in a molecule, and checks its answers against a standard chemistry tool. It then builds a 3D page around it: pick a molecule such as benzene or water, drag a slider to pull it apart, and watch the electrons regroup as the bond breaks. Built for Sovereignty. As organizations build AI around their knowledge and workflows, sovereignty means that they retain control of the models they depend on and the intelligence they create. With Mistral Large 4, that control begins with the model itself. Organizations have the ability to inspect, customize, and deploy the model on their own infrastructure. They can use and improve Mistral Large 4 without depending on Mistral to serve it through an API. Mistral Large 4 was developed and trained from scratch in Europe, giving organizations clarity about the origins of the technology they’re building on. Control also extends to how AI operates inside an organization. Organizations can customize Mistral Large 4 around their proprietary data with Mistral Forge , and they can build, govern, and improve the resulting agents and applications using Mistral Studio. Mistral’s Applied AI experts can work alongside customer teams to build and deploy these tailored systems. Through that work, teams understand the architecture and decisions behind what they’ve built, along with the methods used to train and operate it, so they can run and improve their AI independently. At ABN AMRO, we believe that open and transparent AI ecosystems are essential for driving innovation responsibly within the financial sector. Developments such as Mistral Large 4 demonstrate how sovereign and open-weight AI models can expand the range of trusted solutions available to European organizations. We are encouraged by the progress being made and continue to explore how advanced AI can contribute to strengthening critical capabilities, including cybersecurity. Coen Klaver, Director Cyber Defense at ABN AMRO Bank N.V. The rapid progress we are seeing in AI models creates exciting opportunities for advanced engineering in chip manufacturing. Our early experience with Mistral Large 4 is promising, particularly for use cases where higher model performance matters. Mistral’s commitment to continued innovation supports our efforts to accelerate the application of AI throughout our semiconductor product lifecycle. Arnaud Hubaux, Head of AI Program and Strategy. Mistral Large 4 is an important step forward for financial‑grade AI: an open‑weight model we can fine‑tune to our needs, deploy on our own infrastructure and closely integrate into our digital channels. Hey Belfius is a flagship example of how this partnership helps us rethink how customers interact with their bank. Nicolas Goosse, Head of Data Insights, Analytics & AI at Belfius Mastering our AI begins with mastering its architecture and data. For the most sensitive use cases, having access to European open-weight models, which we can deploy on our own infrastructure, is a vital lever for strengthening our strategic autonomy and the resilience of our organizations. The industrial partnership between Crédit Agricole Artificial Intelligence and Mistral addresses these challenges at the Group level. The "Le Chonk" model, which stands out for its reasoning capabilities and performance in the field of cybersecurity, is a promising illustration of the possibilities opened up by this partnership. Oliver Biton, Group CIO, Crédit Agricole We're excited about an open-weight model with strong scientific and vision capabilities. Our work is highly specialized, so the ability to adapt a model matters. With Mistral Large 4, we see a foundation for building tools around the way our scientists and engineers actually work with Earth observation data — from imagery to technical documents. Giuseppe Borghi, Head of ESA Φ-lab AI sovereignty isn't about choosing which API to call. It's about having the freedom to run, customize, and build AI on your own terms. Mistral Large 4 brings powerful capabilities in coding, multimodal AI, and cybersecurity into the open, giving developers, companies, and countries a great open foundation to build their own AI and defend themselves against cyber threats. Jeff Boudier, VP Product, Hugging Face A powerful model is only part of the equation. Developers also need the freedom to decide where it runs, how it is optimized, and how it fits into their systems. We’re excited about Mistral Large 4 because open weights give builders more control over those decisions, rather than making them dependent on a single hosted service. At ZML, we see that freedom as essential to turning advances in AI into useful, deployable software. Steeve Morin, CEO of ZML Sovereignty does not always require self-hosting; sometimes it just requires deployments that meet your control requirements. For organizations that prefer a managed service, Mistral Large 4 is available through Microsoft Foundry, with private deployment options for Azure developers. Microsoft and Mistral AI share a commitment to expanding customer choice in next-generation AI. As the first cloud provider to bring Mistral Large 4 to customers, Microsoft is making Mistral’s latest open-weight model available through Microsoft Foundry, an enterprise AI platform built for evaluating, deploying, and operating models at scale. For organizations advancing sovereign AI strategies, this combination offers greater flexibility and control across their data, infrastructure, and AI operations. Tina Schuchman, Corporate Vice President, Foundry, Microsoft Start building with Le Chonk Mistral Large 4 is available to try, deploy, and customize today. Get started in Mistral Studio , through the Mistral API , or on OpenRouter . For full control, download the open weights from Hugging Face and deploy on your own infrastructure with vLLM or SGLang. The model card and license have everything you need to get started — and for those who want to go deeper, a full technical report is coming soon. You can also try the new model in Vibe Code ; give it a feature to build or a bug to fix in your own repository. Mistral Large 4, is also available through NVIDIA-hosted endpoints , as an optimized NVIDIA NIM container for serving with vLLM. Developers can use the open source NeMo AutoModel library for customization or the open source TensorRT LLM library for high-throughput serving. Enterprises can also tailor Mistral Large 4 to their proprietary data, use cases, and guardrails with Mistral Forge. Talk to our team to learn more. The model is available to use under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight license , a modified MIT license. The model is free to use, modify, fine-tune, and commercialize, with a single condition: businesses that operate a Model-as-a-Service offering must obtain a separate commercial license from Mistral before using the model commercially. Starting today, Mistral Large 4 is priced at $0.70 input / M, $0.07 cached input / M, and $2.10 output / M tokens. We encourage the community to put Mistral Large 4 to the test. Run your own evaluations, push its limits, and share your findings with us on X , Discord , or GitHub . What's Next Mistral Large 4 will serve as the foundation for a new generation of specialized and optimized Mistral models. Building on recent releases such as Voxtral and Timestral , we'll continue expanding the frontier of open-weight AI, continuing to give developers and enterprises greater freedom to build, customize, and own their intelligence. title: H.264 Is Magic (2016)
body_text: H.264 is magic: a technical walkthrough of a remarkable technology. Sid Bala Home LinkedIn GitHub Sign in Subscribe H.264 is Magic Sid Bala 02 Nov 2016 • 10 min read Share H.264 is a video compression codec standard. It is ubiquitous - internet video, Blu-ray, phones, security cameras, drones, everything. Everything uses H.264 now. H.264 is a remarkable piece of technology. It is the result of 30+ years of work with one single goal: To reduce the bandwidth required for transmission of full-motion video. Technically, it is very interesting. This post will give insight into some of the details at a high level - I hope to not bore you too much with the intricacies. Also note that many of the concepts explained here apply to video compression in general, and not just H.264. Why even compress anything? A simple uncompressed video file will contain an array of 2D buffers containing pixel data for each frame. So it's a 3D (2 spatial dimensions and 1 temporal) array of bytes. Each pixel takes 3 bytes to store - one byte each for the three primary colors (red, green and blue). 1080p @ 60 Hz = 1920x1080x60x3 => ~ 370 MB/sec of raw data. This is next to impossible to deal with. A 50GB Blu-ray disk will only hold ~2 mins. You can't move it anywhere fast. Even SSDs have trouble dumping this straight from RAM to Disk[^1]. So yeah. We need compression. Why H.264 compression? Yes, I will answer this. But first let me show you something. Here is the Apple Homepage: I captured the screen of this home page and produced two files: PNG screenshot of the Apple homepage 1015KB 5 Second 60fps H.264 video of the same Apple homepage 175KB Eh. What? Those file sizes look switched. No, they're right. The H.264 video, 300 frames long is 175KB. A single frame of that video in PNG is 1015KB. It looks like we're storing 300 times the amount of data in the video. But the file size is a fifth. So H.264 would seem to be 1500x as efficient as PNG. How is this even possible? All right, what's the trick? There are very many tricks! H.264 uses all the tricks you can think of (and tons you can't think of). Let's go through the important ones. Shedding weight Imagine you're building a car for street racing. You need to go faster. What is the first thing you do? You shed some weight. Your car weighs 3000 lbs. You throw away stuff you don't need. Those back seats? pfft. Chuck those. That subwoofer? Gone. No music for you. Air Conditioning? Yeah, ditch it. Transmission? Ye..no. Wait! We're gonna need that. You remove everything except the things that matter. This concept of throwing away bits you don't need to save space is called lossy compression. H.264 is a lossy codec - it throws away less important bits and only keeps the important bits. PNG is a lossless codec. It means that nothing is thrown away. Bit for bit, the original source image can be recovered from a PNG encoded image. Important bits? How does the algorithm know what bits in my frame are important? There are few obvious ways to trim out images. Maybe the top right quadrant is useless all the time. So maybe we can zero out those pixels and discard that quadrant. We would use only 3/4th of the space we need. ~2200 lbs now. Or maybe we can crop out a thick border around the edges of the frame, the important stuff is in the middle anyway. Yes, you could do these. But H.264 doesn't do this. What does H.264 actually do? H.264, like other lossy image algorithms, discards detail information. Here is a close-up of the original compared with the image post-discard. See how the compressed one does not show the holes in the speaker grills in the MacBook Pro? If you don't zoom in, you would even notice the difference. The image on the right weighs in at 7% the size of the original - and we haven't even compressed the image in the traditional sense. Imagine your car weighed just 200 lbs! 7% wow! How do you discard detail information like that? For this we need a quick math lesson. Information Entropy Now we're getting to the juicy bits! Ha puns! If you took an information theory class, you might remember information entropy. Information entropy is the number of bits required to represent some information. Note that it is not simply the size of some dataset. It is minimum number of bits that must be used to represent all the information contained in a dataset. For example, if your dataset is the result of a single coin toss, you need 1 bit of entropy. If you have record two coin tosses, you'll need 2 bits. Makes sense? Suppose you have some strange coin - you've tossed it 10 times, and every time it lands on heads. How would you describe this information to someone? You wouldn't say HHHHHHHHH. You would just say "10 tosses, all heads" - bam! You've just compressed some data! Easy. I saved you hours of mindfuck lectures. This is obviously an oversimplification, but you've transformed some data into another shorter representation of the same information. You've reduced data redundancy . The information entropy in this dataset has not changed - you've just converted between representations. This type of encoder is called an entropy encoder - it's a general-purpose lossless encoder that works for any type of data. Frequency Domain Now that you understand information entropy, let's move on to transformations of data. You can represent data in some fundamental units. If you use binary, you have 0 and 1. If you use hex, you have 16 characters. You can easily transform between the two systems. They are essentially equivalent. So far so good? Ok! Now, some imagination! Imagine you can transform any dataset that varies over space(or time) - something like the brightness value of an image, into a different coordinate space. So instead of x-y coordinates, let's say we have frequency coordinates. freqX and freqY are the axes now. This is called a frequency domain representation. There is another mindfuck mathematical theorem[^2] that states that you can do this for any data and you can achieve a perfect lossless transformation as long as freqX and freqY are high enough. Okay, but what the freq are freqX and freqY? freqX and freqY are some other set of basis units. Just like when we switch from binary to hex, we have a different fundamental unit, we're switching from the familiar X-Y to freqX and freqY. Hex 'A' looks different from binary '1010'. Both mean the same thing, but look different. So here is what our image looks like in the frequency domain: The fine grill on that MacBook pro has a high information content in the higher frequency components of that image. Finely varying content = high frequency components. Any sort of gradual variation in the color and brightness - such as gradients are low frequency components of that image. Anything in between falls in between. So fine details = high freq. Gentle gradients = low freq. Makes sense? In the frequency domain representation, the low frequency components are near the center of that image. The higher frequency components are towards of the edges of the image. Okay. Kinda makes sense. But why do all this? Because now, you can take that frequency domain image and then mask out the edges - discard information which will contain the information with high frequency components. Now if you convert back to your regular x-y coordinates, you'll find that the resulting image looks similar to the original but has lost some of the fine details. But now, the image only occupies a fraction of the space. By controlling how big your mask is, you can now tune precisely how detailed you want your output images to be. Here is the close-up of the laptop in the home page again. Except now, there is a circular border mask that's been applied. The numbers represent the information entropy of that image as a fraction of the original. Even at 2%, you won't notice the difference unless you're at this zoom level. 2%! - your car now weighs 60 lbs! So that's how you shed weight. This process in lossy compression is called quantization [^3]. Okay. Impressive, I guess. What else you got? Chroma Subsampling. The human/eye brain system is not very good at resolving finer details in color. It can detect minor variations in brightness very easily but not color. So there must be some way to discard color information to shed even more weight. In a TV signal, R+G+B color data gets transformed to Y+Cb+Cr. The Y is the luminance (essentially black and white brightness) and the Cb and Cr are the chrominance (color) components. RGB and YCbCr are equivalent in terms of information entropy. Why unnecessarily complicate? RGB not good enough for you? Back before we had color TV, we only had the Y signal. And when color TVs just started coming along, engineers had to figure out a way to transmit RGB color along with Y. Instead of using two separate data streams, they wisely decided to encode the color information into Cb and Cr and transmit that along with the Y information. That way, BW TVs would only look at the Y component. Color TVs will, in addition, look at the chrominance components and convert to RGB internally. But check out the trick: the Y component gets encoded at full resolution. The C components only at a quarter resolution. Since the eye/brain is terrible at detecting color variations, you can get away with this. By doing this, you reduce total bandwidth by one half, with very little visual difference. Half! Your car now weighs 30 lbs! This process of discarding some of the color information is called Chroma Subsampling [^4]. While not specific to H.264 and has been around for decades itself, it is used almost universally. Those are the big weight shedders for lossy compression. Our frames are now tiny - since we discarded most of the detail information and half of the color information. Wait. That's it? Can we do something more? Yes. Weight shedding is only the first step. So far we're only looking at the spatial domains within a single frame. Now it's time to explore temporal compression - where we look at a group of frames across time. Motion compensation H.264 is a motion compensation compression standard. Motion compensation? What now? Imagine you're watching a tennis match. The camera is fixed at a certain angle. The only thing moving is the ball back and forth. How would you encode this information? You do what you always do, right? You have a 3D array of pixels, two dimensions in space and one in time. Right? Nah. Why would you? Most of the image is the same anyway. The court, the net, the crowds, all are static. The only real action is the ball moving. What if you could just have one static image of everything in the background, and then one moving image of just the ball? Wouldn't that save a lot of space? You see where I am going with this? Get it? See where I am going? Motion estimation? Lame jokes aside, this is exactly what H.264 does. H.264 splits up the image into macro-blocks - typically 16x16 pixel blocks that it will use for motion estimation. It encodes one static image - typically called an I-frame (Intra frame). This is a full frame - containing all the bits it required to construct that frame. And then subsequent frames are either P-frames (predicted) or B-frames (bi-directionally predicted). P-frames are frames that will encode a motion vector for each of the macro-blocks from the previous frame. So a P-frame has to be constructed by the decoder based on previous frames. It starts with the last I-frame in the video stream and then walks through every subsequent frame - adding up the motion vector deltas as it goes along until it arrives at the current frame. B-frames are even more interesting, where the prediction happens bi-directionally, both from past frames and from future frames. So you can imagine now why that Apple home page video is so well compressed. Because it's really just three I-frames in which the macro blocks are being panned around. Let's say you've been playing a video on YouTube. You missed the last few seconds of dialog, so you scrub back a few seconds. Have you noticed that it doesn't instantly start playing from that timecode you just selected. It pauses for a few moments and then plays. It's already buffered those frames from the network, since you just played it, so why that pause? Yeah that annoys the shit out of me. Why does it do that? Because you've asked the decoder to jump to some arbitrary frame, the decoder has to redo all the calculations - starting from the nearest I-frames and adding up the motion vector deltas to the frame you're on - and this is computationally expensive, and hence the brief pause. Hopefully you'll be less annoyed now, knowing it's actually doing hard work and not just sitting around just to annoy you. Since you're only encoding motion vectors deltas, this technique is extremely space-efficient for any video with motion, at the cost of some computation. Now we've covered both spatial and temporal compression! So far we have a shitton of space saved in Quantization. Chroma subsampling further halved the space required. On top of that, we have motion compensation that stores only 3 actual frames for the ~300 that we had in that video. Looks pretty good to me. Now what? Now we wrap up and seal the deal. We use a traditional lossless entropy encoder. Because why not? Let's just slap that on there for good measure. Entropy Coder The I-frames, after the lossy steps, contain redundant information. The motion vectors for each of the macro blocks in the P and B-frames - there are entire groups of them with the same values - since several macro blocks move by the same amount when the image pans in our test video. An entropy encoder will take care of this redundancy. And since it is a general purpose lossless encoder, we don't have to worry about what tradeoffs it's making. We can recover all the data that goes in. And, we're done! At the core of it, this is how video compression codecs like H.264 work. These are its tricks. Ok great! But I am curious to know how much our car weighs now. The original video was captured at an odd resolution of 1232x1154. If we apply the math here, we get: 5 secs @ 60 fps = 1232x1154x60x3x5 => 1.2 GB Compressed video => 175 KB If we apply the same ratio to our 3000 lb car, we get 0.4 lbs as the final weight. 6.5 ounces! Yeah. It's magic! Obviously, I am massively oversimplifying several decades of intense research in this field. If you want to know more, the Wikipedia Page is pretty descriptive. Have comments? Did I get something wrong? Not a fan of the lame jokes? Offended by the swearing? Use HackerNews or Reddit for voicing your opinion! Or hit me up on Twitter or LinkedIn if you want to chat. [^1] SSD Benchmarks [^2] Nyquist-Shannon Sampling Theorem [^3][Quantization]( https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantization_(signal_processing) [^4] Chroma Subsampling Sign up for more like this. title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart
body_text: DoorDash to Acquire Instacart to Help Local Stores Win | DoorDash DoorDash DoorDash Products Company Impact Advertise News Blog Help English (US) Español (US) English (CA) Français (CA) English (AU) English (NZ) US Get Started News Announcements Culture Policy Trends & Insights Archives Categories Announcements Culture Policy Trends & Insights Archives Announcements DoorDash to Acquire Instacart to Help Local Stores Win Together, DoorDash and Instacart would help stores of every size reach more customers with the kinds of innovative technology that the biggest online retailers and grocers build for themselves. Oct 29, 2026 Transaction values Instacart at $65.00 per share, representing a 26% premium to Instacart's closing price on October 22, 2026 Together, DoorDash and Instacart would help stores of every size reach more customers with the kinds of innovative technology that the biggest online retailers and grocers build for themselves Consumers to benefit from more choice and access to affordable delivery and savings Dashers and Shoppers to have more earnings opportunities and more choice over when and how they earn DoorDash, Inc. (NASDAQ: DASH) and Maplebear Inc. (d.b.a. Instacart, NASDAQ: CART) today announced a definitive agreement under which DoorDash will acquire Instacart for a total value of $65.00 for each Instacart share, or an equity value of approximately $17 billion. The aggregate transaction consideration will be at least 75% cash, with Instacart stockholders able to elect cash, DoorDash stock, or a combination of both, subject to proration so that DoorDash stock does not exceed 25% of the aggregate consideration. Instacart's board of directors has unanimously approved the agreement. DoorDash and Instacart share a mission to help local businesses succeed. Families turn to Instacart for the big weekly shop and to DoorDash for meals and nearly anything else they need from their neighborhood in under an hour. The combined company will offer grocers and retailers of every size DoorDash's delivery network and Instacart's grocery and fulfillment technology, in both apps and on stores' own websites, along with the advertising and AI tools each company has built. On either app, customers pick a store in their own community, and the store makes the sale. Consumers will have more stores to choose from, more savings opportunities when they choose to shop with a local business, and faster delivery options, while Dashers and Shoppers will have more ways to earn. Most grocery shopping still happens in stores, but more people are buying groceries and everyday goods online. They expect fast, affordable delivery and an easy way to order. The biggest online retailers and grocers are racing ahead, building their own delivery fleets, warehouses, membership programs, and AI shopping assistants. A grocer or retailer running on thin margins cannot build all of that alone, and with AI, the playing field risks being tilted even further away from local commerce. DoorDash and Instacart believe that communities benefit when Main Street competes, and they build the tools that empower local businesses. Together, they could help local stores grow online. More grocers could deploy Instacart's technology to run their own websites and retail media networks, bringing them more sales and advertising revenue. Brands would gain a scaled alternative for reaching customers online. Grocers could add capacity for online orders through DoorDash's DashMart Fulfillment Services and offer faster, more accurate, and more affordable delivery. “Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online. Someone has to pick a ripe avocado, find a substitute you’d choose yourself, and get the ice cream to you before it melts,” said Tony Xu, co-founder and CEO of DoorDash. “Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day. Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery. It’s still early innings, but we know that when more people shop local, more dollars stay local.” “Over the last 14 years, Instacart has transformed online grocery by helping retailers of all sizes compete and grow, and joining forces with DoorDash allows us to do even more,” said Chris Rogers, CEO of Instacart. “When our purpose-built grocery technology and trusted retailer and brand relationships are combined with DoorDash’s global consumer reach and logistics capabilities, we can create new opportunities for our retail and brand partners, offer an even better experience for customers and shoppers, and deliver compelling value for our shareholders. Together, we can accelerate innovation across the grocery industry and make online grocery more seamless and affordable for the millions of households we serve.” Benefits and commitments DoorDash expects many benefits will flow from the transaction, including: More Choice for Consumers : Instacart customers could shop at more than 50,000 additional stores, on top of the nearly 100,000 stores on the Instacart platform today. Two Memberships for the Price of One : DashPass and Instacart+ members would pay one membership fee instead of two, which would save them an estimated $100 million per year on membership fees alone. More Ways to Earn for Dashers and Shoppers : More orders for local businesses can create more earning opportunities, with more choice over when and how they earn, whether that’s grocery orders on a quiet day, restaurant orders at peak times, or both. DoorDash is proud to share a few of the post-close commitments it is making today that demonstrate how this deal benefits local communities: Open Platform, No Grocery Exclusivity : Local grocers can work with any delivery platform they choose to help them grow. Shoppers Keep What They Love : Instacart Shoppers can keep the features they love, including the flexibility to choose how much they work and the information they need to decide which batches to accept, and choose whether to take on DoorDash orders or keep shopping only on Instacart. Following closing, DoorDash is expected to keep Instacart’s brand, enterprise technology products, and app. Until the transaction closes, DoorDash and Instacart will continue to operate as separate and independent companies. Transaction details The value of $65.00 per Instacart share represents a 26% premium to Instacart's closing price on October 22, 2026, the last trading day before media reports about a possible transaction. Instacart stockholders will have the right to elect to receive, for each Instacart share: (i) $65.00 in cash, (ii) 0.3372 shares of DoorDash common stock, or (iii) a mix of $48.75 in cash and 0.0843 shares of DoorDash common stock, in each case, subject to a cap on the total stock consideration issuable by DoorDash equal to 25% of the aggregate consideration and certain proration mechanics. If stock consideration is oversubscribed, applicable Instacart stockholders will receive stock consideration on a prorated basis. DoorDash expects to fund the cash portion of the consideration with cash on hand and proceeds from debt financing. DoorDash has entered into a financing commitment letter with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. providing for a 364-day senior unsecured bridge loan facility in support of the debt component of the transaction, subject to satisfaction or waiver of certain customary conditions. The transaction is not subject to a financing condition. DoorDash is targeting a capital structure that will maintain investment-grade ratings. The transaction is expected to close in the end of 2027 or the first half of 2028, subject to approval by Instacart stockholders, the expiration or termination of the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, other regulatory approvals, including in Canada and Israel, and other customary closing conditions. Stockholders holding about 19% of Instacart's outstanding shares have agreed to vote in favor of the transaction. Conference call DoorDash will separately report its third quarter 2026 results today and will discuss the transaction on its earnings call at 5:30 a.m. PT (8:30 a.m. ET). The webcast and transaction materials are available at ir.doordash.com. Advisors Centerview Partners LLC is acting as lead financial advisor to DoorDash, and J.P. Morgan Securities LLC is also acting as a financial advisor to DoorDash. Latham & Watkins LLP is serving as legal counsel to DoorDash. JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. acted as sole lead arranger and bookrunner on the committed bridge financing. Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC is acting as financial advisor to Instacart, and Cravath, Swaine & Moore LLP and Cooley LLP are serving as legal counsel to Instacart. About DoorDash DoorDash is building the future of local commerce by connecting people to the best of their neighborhoods. Since our founding in 2013, we have facilitated over 10 billion consumer orders, driven over $230 billion in sales for merchants, helped Dashers earn over $80 billion through the platform, and expanded to more than 40 countries. We support businesses of all sizes through multiple brands around the globe, including DoorDash, Deliveroo, SevenRooms, and Wolt. About Instacart Instacart is a leading grocery technology company that partners with more than 2,200 retail banners – representing nearly 100,000 stores – to transform how people shop for the groceries they need from the retailers they trust, while creating flexible earning opportunities for shoppers. Through the Instacart Marketplace, Instacart Enterprise platform, and Instacart Ads ecosystem, the company powers ecommerce, fulfillment, in-store technology, AI offerings, and advertising for partners. For more information, visit www.instacart.com/company . Maplebear Inc. is the registered corporate name of Instacart. Forward-Looking Statements This release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, which statements involve substantial risks and uncertainties. Forward-looking statements generally relate to future events or the future financial or operating performance of DoorDash, Inc. (“DoorDash”) or Maplebear Inc. (“Instacart”). Forward-looking statements in this release include, but are not limited to, statements regarding the proposed acquisition of Instacart by DoorDash pursuant to the Agreement and Plan of Merger among DoorDash, Ibiza Merger Sub, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of DoorDash, and Instacart (the “Merger Agreement” and such transaction, the “Proposed Transaction”); the expected financing of the Proposed Transaction; the expected timing and likelihood of completion of the Proposed Transaction on the terms contemplated or at all; the expected benefits, synergies, and strategic value of the Proposed Transaction, including the future financial and operating performance of the combined company; DoorDash’s plans and expectations regarding the integration of Instacart; and the plans, objectives, expectations, and intentions of DoorDash and Instacart with respect to the Proposed Transaction, the period of pendency of the Proposed Transaction, and the combined company. These expectations and beliefs may not materialize, and actual results in future periods are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those projected, including risks and uncertainties related to: the occurrence of any event, change, or other circumstance that could give rise to the termination of the Merger Agreement, including circumstances requiring a party to pay a termination fee or reimburse expenses; the ability to obtain, or delays in obtaining, governmental and regulatory approvals required for the Proposed Transaction, including the expiration or termination of the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended, and any required clearance or approval under the Competition Act (Canada) or under the Israeli Economic Competition Law-1988, and the risk that such approvals may result in the imposition of conditions that could adversely affect the combined company or the expected benefits of the Proposed Transaction; the ability to obtain the requisite approval of Instacart stockholders; the satisfaction or waiver of the other conditions to the closing of the Proposed Transaction; delays in completing the Proposed Transaction, or the failure to complete the Proposed Transaction at all; the ability to obtain adequate financing or financings on satisfactory terms and the effect of any indebtedness incurred in connection with the Proposed Transaction on the combined company’s credit ratings; the ability to successfully integrate Instacart’s business and to realize the anticipated cost savings, synergies, and other benefits of the Proposed Transaction within the expected timeframe or at all; the effect of any announcement relating to the Proposed Transaction on the market price of DoorDash’s or Instacart’s common stock; fluctuations in the market price of DoorDash common stock and the possibility that Instacart stockholders may receive a form of consideration different from what they elect as a result of proration; the nature, cost, and outcome of any litigation related to the Proposed Transaction; the risk that the Proposed Transaction disrupts current plans and operations or diverts management’s attention from ongoing business operations and opportunities; adverse reactions or changes to business or employee relationships resulting from the announcement, pendency, or completion of the Proposed Transaction; the ability of DoorDash and Instacart to retain and hire key personnel; economic, financial, social, or political conditions that could adversely affect DoorDash or Instacart; the macroeconomic environment and geopolitical uncertainty; competition; changes in legislation or governmental regulations; legal proceedings and regulatory matters and developments; and DoorDash’s and Instacart’s respective brands and reputations. The forward-looking statements contained in this release are also subject to other risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ from the results predicted, including those more fully described in the filings of DoorDash and Instacart with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”), including DoorDash’s and Instacart’s respective Annual Reports on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 and quarterly reports on Form 10-Q filed thereafter, as well as in the registration statement on Form S-4 and the proxy statement/prospectus described below when they become available. All forward-looking statements in this release are based on information available to DoorDash and Instacart and assumptions and beliefs as of the date hereof, and each of DoorDash and Instacart disclaims any obligation to update any forward-looking statements, except as required by law. Important Additional Information Will Be Filed with the SEC and Where to Find It In connection with the Proposed Transaction, DoorDash intends to file with the SEC a registration statement on Form S-4 (the “Registration Statement”) to register the shares of DoorDash common stock to be issued in connection with the Proposed Transaction. The Registration Statement will include a proxy statement of Instacart that also constitutes a prospectus of DoorDash (the “proxy statement/prospectus”). Each of DoorDash and Instacart may also file other relevant documents with the SEC regarding the Proposed Transaction. After the Registration Statement has been declared effective by the SEC, a definitive proxy statement/prospectus will be mailed to stockholders of Instacart as of the record date established for voting on the Proposed Transaction. This release is not a substitute for the Registration Statement, the proxy statement/prospectus, or any other document that DoorDash or Instacart may file with the SEC in connection with the Proposed Transaction. INVESTORS AND SECURITY HOLDERS OF DOORDASH AND INSTACART ARE URGED TO READ THE REGISTRATION STATEMENT, INCLUDING THE PROXY STATEMENT/PROSPECTUS AND DOCUMENTS INCORPORATED THEREIN BY REFERENCE, AND ANY OTHER RELEVANT DOCUMENTS THAT ARE FILED OR WILL BE FILED WITH THE SEC, AS WELL AS ANY AMENDMENTS OR SUPPLEMENTS TO THOSE DOCUMENTS, CAREFULLY AND IN THEIR ENTIRETY IF AND WHEN THEY BECOME AVAILABLE BECAUSE THEY WILL CONTAIN IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT DOORDASH, INSTACART, THE PROPOSED TRANSACTION, THE RISKS RELATED THERETO, AND RELATED MATTERS. Investors and security holders will be able to obtain free copies of the Registration Statement and the proxy statement/prospectus (when available), as each may be amended or supplemented from time to time, and other documents containing important information about DoorDash, Instacart, and the Proposed Transaction, once such documents are filed with the SEC, through the website maintained by the SEC at www.sec.gov . Copies of the documents filed with the SEC by DoorDash, including the proxy statement/prospectus (when available), will be available free of charge on DoorDash’s investor relations website at ir.doordash.com. Copies of the documents filed with the SEC by Instacart, including the proxy statement/prospectus (when available), will be available free of charge on Instacart’s investor relations website at investors.instacart.com. Participants in the Solicitation DoorDash, Instacart, and certain of their respective directors, executive officers, and other members of management and employees may be deemed to be participants in the solicitation of proxies from Instacart’s stockholders in respect of the Proposed Transaction under the rules of the SEC. Information about the directors and executive officers of DoorDash, including a description of their direct or indirect interests, by security holdings or otherwise, is set forth in DoorDash’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, its definitive proxy statement on Schedule 14A for its 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders, and its definitive information statement on Schedule 14C filed with the SEC on August 27, 2026 (including the beneficial ownership information set forth therein), each filed with the SEC. Information about the directors and executive officers of Instacart, including a description of their direct or indirect interests, by security holdings or otherwise, is set forth in Instacart’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 and its definitive proxy statement on Schedule 14A for its 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders, each filed with the SEC. To the extent holdings of securities by the directors and executive officers of DoorDash or Instacart have changed from the amounts reflected therein, such changes have been or will be reflected on Initial Statements of Beneficial Ownership of Securities on Form 3, Statements of Changes in Beneficial Ownership on Form 4, or Annual Statements of Changes in Beneficial Ownership of Securities on Form 5 subsequently filed with the SEC. Other information regarding the interests of participants in the proxy solicitation, which may differ from the interests of DoorDash and Instacart stockholders generally, will be contained in the Registration Statement, the proxy statement/prospectus, and other relevant materials to be filed with the SEC regarding the Proposed Transaction when they become available. Investors and security holders should read the proxy statement/prospectus carefully when it becomes available before making any voting or investment decisions. You may obtain free copies of these documents from DoorDash or Instacart using the sources indicated above.
